summary: H.R. 6575, titled the 'CommonGround for Affordable Health Care Act', amends the Internal Revenue Code and the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act. It extends and modifies enhanced health insurance premium tax credits for 2026, establishes fraud prevention guardrails and verification processes for Affordable Care Act exchanges and broker-assisted enrollments, extends the annual open enrollment period for plan year 2026, places new reporting and transparency requirements on pharmacy benefit managers in Medicare Part D, and sets expedited legislative procedures for future premium tax credit reform bills.

affected_groups.effect: Qualifies individuals for extended enhanced premium tax credits through 2026, broadens income eligibility tiers up to 1000 percent of the poverty line, requires clear advance notification of credit values, and protects against unauthorized enrollment changes.
affected_groups.group: Health insurance exchange enrollees and taxpayers

affected_groups.effect: Subject to stricter verification requirements, marketing oversight, mandatory standards of conduct, civil penalties ranging from $10,000 to $200,000 for negligence or fraud, and criminal penalties including up to 10 years imprisonment.
affected_groups.group: Insurance agents, brokers, and marketing organizations

affected_groups.effect: Required to limit remuneration to bona fide service fees, pass through certain rebates and discounts, submit detailed annual transparency and drug utilization reports, and comply with annual independent audits starting in 2029.
Must contractually enforce PBM transparency and fee rules, collect disgorged funds, submit annual compliance certifications, and maintain anti-retaliation mechanisms.
affected_groups.group: Medicare Part D and Medicare Advantage plan sponsors

key_provisions: Extends and modifies temporary premium tax credit percentage tables and income eligibility rules up to 1000 percent of the poverty line for taxable year 2026.

Imposes civil and criminal penalties on agents and brokers who provide negligent or knowing false information on exchange applications, and establishes verification requirements for agent-assisted enrollments.
Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services to periodically check the Death Master File to remove deceased individuals from exchange health plans.
Extends the annual open enrollment period for the 2026 plan year to run from November 1, 2025, through March 19, 2026.
Establishes new transparency, reporting, fee restrictions, and audit rules for pharmacy benefit managers operating in Medicare Part D and Medicare Advantage prescription drug plans starting in 2029.
Creates expedited committee and floor consideration rules in the House and Senate for qualifying enhanced premium tax credit reform bills up to July 1, 2026.

summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 6575, titled the 'CommonGround for Affordable Health Care Act', amends the Internal Revenue Code and the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act. It extends and modifies enhanced health insurance premium tax credits for 2026, establishes fraud prevention guardrails and verification processes for Affordable Care Act exchanges and broker-assisted enrollments, extends the annual open enrollment period for plan year 2026, places new reporting and transparency requirements on pharmacy benefit managers in Medicare Part D, and sets expedited legislative procedures for future premium tax credit reform bills.
summary_detail.significance: The bill alters federal healthcare financing by extending expanded health insurance subsidies for a year, introduces wide-ranging regulatory compliance and fraud controls for insurance brokers and exchanges, and places extensive reporting and financial restrictions on pharmacy benefit managers within Medicare drug programs.
